figures.caption: Table 3: Main results on Epic-Kitchens-100. Top-1 and Top-5 accuracy for verb, noun, and composed action across three VLMs. Graphs + ICL uses one in-context example per class with 100 candidate classes; Overall reports the macro-average over the three models per modality. ICL entries are mean ± SEM over 5 seeds.

Figure 3: ICL scaling on EGTEA across different model parameter regimes (MCA). The horizontal dashed lines indicate the 0-shot raw frame baseline for each respective model. This visualizes the crossover point: while 0-shot graphs occasionally underperform dense frame inputs, scaling to k ≥ 1 graph examples consistently eclipses the frames-only bounds across nearly all tested architectures.

Table 6: Vision-Language Models evaluated. Eleven instruction-tuned VLMs from six open-weight families, grouped into three size regimes. MoE rows report total / active parameters; dense rows report total. Context lengths are the native pre-training windows reported by the model authors. Models marked ∗ run from quantized checkpoints to fit inference within four L40S GPUs. All models are evaluated with reasoning modes disabled and greedy decoding (T =0).

Table 7: EGTEA action recognition across models and input modalities. We report MCA, Top-1, Top-3, and Top-5 accuracy. Within each model block, the best entry per metric is shown in bold, and the second-best is underlined; the modality with the highest average across the four metrics is

Figure 4: ICL scaling on Epic-Kitchens-100 across Verb, Noun, and Action (Top-1). Each panel reports Top-1 accuracy as a function of the number of graph-based in-context examples provided per class (0 corresponds to the graphs-only setting, i.e., no in-context demonstrations). Solid lines denote 50 candidate classes; dashed lines, 100. Long-dashed horizontals mark the frames-only baseline.

Table 4: TAG construction ablation on EGTEA. Joint ablation over overlapping windows (Window), multi-stage prompting (MS-Prompt.), and node attributes (Attr.) on two Qwen3.5 backbones. The last row of each block is the full configuration.

Table 8: Epic-Kitchens-100 action recognition across models and input modalities. We report Top-1 and Top-5 accuracy for verb, noun, and action prediction; legend conventions follow Table 7. ICL rows sweep the number of in-context examples per class (k∈ {1, 2}) and the candidate-set size (50 or 100 classes), and report mean ± SEM over 5 demonstration draws. The Overall block macro-averages each modality across models.

Figure 5: Qualitative results of TAG on EGTEA and Epic-Kitchens-100. For each clip (rows), we show four sampled frames and the predicted label under Frames only, Graphs only, and Graphs + ICL, with correct predictions in green and errors in red. The temporal graph Gτ already resolves several verb-level errors made under Frames only, and adding in-context examples further disambiguates fine-grained verb and noun confusions that persist in the Graphs only variant. Results obtained with Qwen3.5-122B* on EGTEA and GLM-4.6V* on Epic-Kitchens-100.
